sentences.text: T his case emanates from a private complaint filed by the complainant alleging that the accused has committed the offence punishable under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, by issuing cheque for an amount of Rs.16,00,000/-, as the same was dishonored.

2. THE BRIEF FACTS;
It is the case of the complainant that it is a company incorporated under the provisions of the Companies Act and licensed by the Reserve Bank of India.
It is involved in the business of providing financial facilities for the needy persons for purchasing motor vehicles.
It is functioning in the address stated in the cause title.

The accused had approached the complainant seeking for financial assistance of Rs.16,00,000/- for procuring a TATA LPT 909 EX vehicle bearing No.KA53, A5118 vehicle and thereby entered into Loan agreement bearing No.1805472 and the accused had agreed to abide by Judgment CC No.29187/2018 KABC030792642018 3:-
-:
the terms and conditions of agreement and also agreed to pay the monthly installment without delay/default.

The accused has been a chronic defaulter in making the monthly installment and as such a huge amount has been accrued to accused account as outstanding by way of unpaid monthly installment charges and delay/late charges applicable as per the terms and conditions of the complainant.
Despite repeated and personal follow up by the complainant and the representatives of the complainant, the accused had failed and neglected to make payment.
As per the loan agreement a huge amount was payable by accused.

In lieu of the same,
accused approached the complainant towards the total amount payable and had issued a cheque bearing No.002990 dated 04.08.2018 for a sum of Rs.16,00,000/-.
On the instructions of the accused, when the said cheque was presented by the complainant for encashment, same was returned with an endorsement as ' I n s u f f i c i e n t F u n d s ' .

Again on same copy of legal notice sent, but it was returned "un-served" dated 15.09.2018.
In-spite of the same, accused has not come forward to make payment for the cheque amount and accused has intentionally issued the cheque without maintaining sufficient balance in his account.

sentences.text: However, it is well settled that whenever complainant alleged that the accused has committed an offence punishable U/Sec.138 of N.I. Act, obviously, the complainant has to establish that there was a legally enforceable debt and to discharge the said legally enforceable debt, the accused has issued the cheque and subsequently the said cheque has been dishonored.
Keeping in view of these main and important ingredients of section 138 of N.I. Act, proceed to discuss the evidence available on record.
As already been stated above, the complainant has examined its Partner as PW.1.

He has filed affidavit in lieu of his examination in chief U/Sec.145 of N.I. Act reiterating the entire averments of the complaint and got marked Ex.P.1 to 21.

On perusal of Ex.P.3, makes it clear that it supports the stand taken by the complainant.
As per clause (a) of proviso to Sec.138 of N.I. Act the cheque is to be presented for encashment within the period of its validity from the date on which the cheque has been issued.
The Ex.P.3 cheque bears the date 04.08.2018 and it was presented on 13.08.2018, which is within the prescribed period.

13. As per clause (b) of proviso to Sec. 138 of N.I. Act, the complainant is required to issue notice, in writing, to the drawer/accused making a demand for repayment of the said cheque amount within 30 days from the date of receipt of information about the dishonor of the cheque.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of Legal notice, Ex.P.6 is the postal receipt, Ex.P.7 is the postal cover.

Thereby, it is found that the complainant has issued legal notice within 30 days from the date of knowledge Judgment CC M/S Mahindra And Mahindra Financial ... vs Gopal Krishna on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43834711/

sentences.text: Thus, the provisions of clause (a) & (b) of proviso to Sec.138 of N.I. Act have been complied with.
14. As per clause (c) of the proviso to Sec. 138 of N.I. Act, the drawer/accused is entitled to have 15 days time to make the payment of the cheque amount.
Even after elapse of 15 days time for making payment the accused has not made payment.
Further the clause (b) of Sec. 142 of N.I. Act makes it clear that the complaint has to be filed within 30 days from the date of cause of action arose.
The endorsement made by this Court on the complaint reveals that the complainant presented the complaint on 10.10.2018 and as such, this complaint is well within the period of limitation.
Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that the complainant has complied all the necessary components which attracts section 138 of N.I. Act.
Even the accused has not challenged any of the mandatory requirements to be complied by the complainant.

As per the Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme in case of APS FOREX SERVICES PRIVATE LTD., vs. SHAKTI INTERNATIONAL FASHION LINKERS AND ORS.,
reported in [2020] ACR 457 wherein it is held that, once accused has admitted issuance of cheque which bears his signature, there is presumption that there exists legally enforceable debt or liability under Sec.139 of N.I. Act.

sentences.text: In the present case the issuance of the cheque and the signature on the cheque is not disputed nor contested by the accused.
The said decision is aptly applicable for raising presumption in favour of complainant.
16. Therefore, when once it is proved that the cheque belonged to the accused coupled with proof that the cheque bears the signature of the accused.
The presumption must be that the cheque was issued for a legally enforceable debt or liability.

As this Court holds that the complainant has proved the execution of Ex.P.3,
cheque and the accused failed to Judgment CC No.29187/2018 KABC030792642018 11:-
-:
rebut the presumption then this Court has to draw a presumption that the cheque has been drawn for lawful consideration.

As a result, the presumption U/sec.139 of N.I.
Act is drawn in favour of complainant.

sentences.text: The accused has not rebutted the presumption raised against him.
The accused has not cross-examined the complainant witness nor challenged the documents exhibited by the complainant.
Even the accused has not led the defence side evidence.
There is nothing on record to doubt the case of the complainant and documents.
In view of the same there is absolutely no embargo to consider the case of the complainant to hold that the accused is guilty of the alleged offence.

18. It is now fairly settled by catena of decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court that the presumption under Section 139 of the N.I. Act extends even to the existence of the debt and it is for the drawer of the said cheque to rebut the said presumption.

Of course, it is also fairly well-settled that the Judgment CC No.29187/2018 KABC030792642018 12:-
-:
accused is not required to prove his defence beyond reasonable doubt.
The standard of proof regarding the defence plea is one of preponderance of probabilities.
But in the present case the accused has even failed to establish preponderance of probability of defence in his favour nor to create a doubt about the case of the complainant.

19. From the evidence on record, it is clear that the accused has failed to rebut the presumption and complainant has proved the existence of the legally recoverable debt and also issuance of cheque for discharge of the said debt.
Admittedly the complainant has complied with all requirements of Section 138 of the N.I. Act.
The statutory notice as required by law had been issued.
The version of complainant is certain and stands proved.
Hence, the above point is answered accordingly.

20. On Point No. 2 : In view of the above findings the accused is found guilty for the offence punishable under Judgment CC No.29187/2018 KABC030792642018 13:-
-:
Section 138 of N.I. Act.
It is just and proper to sentence the accused to pay fine equivalent to the cheque amount along with appropriate penalty.

Thereby, proceed to pass the following:
:: ORDER ::

In exercise of Sec. 264 of Cr.P.C., the accused is convicted for the offence punishable U/Sec. 138 of N.I. Act and sentenced to pay fine of Rs.16,20,000/-, and in default of payment of fine the accused is sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of six months.
